translation_notes: literal islands replace five of the seven Literal(...) calls: Literal("42", datatype=XSD.integer) -> "42"^^xsd:integer, Literal("a string", lang="en") -> "a string"@en, and Literal("whatever", datatype=URIRef("http://example.org/myDatatype")) -> "whatever"^^<http://example.org/myDatatype> (datatype written as a full IRI island)

Literal(42) and Literal("plain string") must stay as calls: outside a g{} island a bare 42 or "plain string" is a Python int/str, and a plain (untagged, untyped) literal has no island form there. This is exactly the documented `Literal(expr) nu hors ilot` limitation, and it shows up inside a list of literals where its five neighbours *did* become islands

NEGATIVE FINDING: `np.assertion += g{ ... }` does not work here. np.assertion is a read-only property of Nanopub, and Python's augmented assignment rebinds the target, so the transpiled `np.assertion = np.assertion.__iadd__(...)` raises AttributeError. The add() call is therefore kept and the islands sit in term positions inside the triple tuple — which also keeps the region's structure intact. The `+=` idiom is only available when the graph is reachable through an assignable name (as np._assertion is in the TestSign.test_sign_errors region of the same file)
prefix declared for XSD only; the draft's dc/rdf/dcterms/prov prefixes are unused in this region and were dropped (they had also been spliced into the middle of the import list)
